title: Monitor Object

validation.research: Five primary sources: Douglas C. Schmidt’s original Monitor Object paper, the authors’ POSA Volume 2 catalog, official Python Condition and queue documentation, and official Java Object.wait/notification documentation. Thread-safe Passive Object is preserved as the established alias. Caller-thread execution, monitor lock, synchronized methods, condition predicates, release/reacquire, notification without immediate lock handoff, invariants before waiting, and runtime-specific semantics are explicit. The inbox, byte limits, closing policy, code, and diagrams are original teaching material.

runnable_example.verification: Exact three-line demo output; the monitor creates no worker and methods execute on real caller threads; positive integer capacities reject Boolean/invalid values, immutable 0/8-byte and binary payloads pass, and invalid items leave protected state unchanged; actual Condition instrumentation proves waiting releases the shared lock, notification while holding it does not transfer ownership, wait returns with the lock reacquired, and extra notifications cause both empty-get and full-put while loops to wait again; space creation unblocks a producer, and preexisting data works without a stored notification; closure wakes all three blocked consumers and all three blocked producers, rejects late puts and preserves accepted buffered data for FIFO drain; twelve close/put races preserve exactly accepted data; three producers and three consumers transfer 90 distinct items at each of capacities one and two, with actual deque instrumentation proving protected mutations, no overlapping mutation, exact accepted/removal FIFO order, capacity bounds, and caller-thread execution without assuming processing order or fairness; repeated close, independent monitors, final empty buffers and all caller-thread joins are verified. Instrumentation wraps real Condition/deque seams and leaves the article methods intact. No deadlines, cancellation, durable delivery, acknowledgment, general rollback, cross-monitor atomicity, or recovery after consumer failure is inferred.

example_limits: Original Python 3.11+ synchronous bounded inbox with real caller threads and no monitor-owned worker. One Condition with one plain nonreentrant Lock protects a deque and closed flag. Capacity is a positive integer item count; payloads are immutable bytes of length 0–8. Predicate checks and mutations share the lock, while loops recheck after wait, and notify_all serves both waiter classes and closure. Close rejects later puts, wakes blocked callers, and preserves accepted items for FIFO removal before Closed. The demonstration creates and joins its own non-daemon consumer; closing the monitor does not join clients or acknowledge outside job processing. Tests verify actual lock release/reacquisition, no notification-time ownership transfer, extra-wakeup loops, blocked full/empty callers, invalid input, close races, independent monitors, and 180 concurrent transferred items across capacities one and two. Removal FIFO is distinct from processing order and waiter fairness. No timeout/deadline, cancellation, durable delivery, acknowledgment, consumer-failure recovery, general rollback, cross-monitor atomicity, or starvation guarantee. Slow work and callbacks belong outside the protected region.
